questions.q: Give an account of the traditional theatre and drama traditions of India.
answer: India has an ancient and varied tradition of theatre, rooted in the Natyashastra of Bharata Muni, which set out the art of drama and the theory of rasa.

answer.text: Sanskrit theatre reached great heights with playwrights such as Kalidasa, whose Abhijnana Shakuntalam is famous, and Shudraka, author of Mrichchhakatika. These plays blended dialogue, music, dance and gesture.

Every region developed its own theatre. Kutiyattam of Kerala is the oldest surviving Sanskrit theatre, while Ramlila enacts the Ramayana in the north; both are recognised by UNESCO. Other forms include Yakshagana in Karnataka, Tamasha in Maharashtra, Jatra in Bengal and Bhaona in Assam, founded by Sankaradeva.
These forms, usually performed in the open, combined storytelling, song, humour and devotion, serving both to entertain and to teach.

answer: Together they form a rich and living theatrical heritage.

questions.q: How does traditional Indian theatre combine music, dance and drama?

answer.text: does not separate acting from music and dance — it weaves them into a single performance.

list: A performance uses spoken words, song, rhythmic movement and stylised gesture together
Forms like Ramlila and Raslila in the north enact the stories of Rama and Krishna through dialogue, music and dance

list: Yakshagana of Karnataka and Kutiyattam of Kerala combine elaborate costume, music and dance-drama
This union of the arts, rooted in the ancient Natyashastra, is the special character of Indian theatre

questions.q: What role has folk and street theatre played in Indian society?

answer.text: have long carried entertainment, devotion and social messages to ordinary people.

list: Forms like Nautanki, Tamasha and Jatra brought stories, humour and song to villages and towns
They needed no grand stage and could be performed anywhere for large gatherings

answer.text: Theatre could teach and move people.

list: They spread religious tales, moral lessons and news among the illiterate
In modern times, street theatre (nukkad natak) has been used to raise awareness on social issues and inspire change
